title: AI Motion Test
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/d3a0e7b89b3248cf909bcfe95c789c95diff%20growth-03.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/ec6ac273f5974ec094f8cf0da61872eediff%20growth-03.jpg)**_✨From 7 Still Images to Animated Fashion Piece (Kling AI)✨_**

**For this experiment, I started with a garment created in CLO3D, rendered the final look in KeyShot, and then generated motion using Kling AI from 7 still frames:**

<https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/adfa298ac9484299ac63cbbbc1181e89>

## _CLO3D → KeyShot → 7 Renders → Kling AI → Video Generation_

![77ad2f15fc174369904f357dd3406000](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/77ad2f15fc174369904f357dd3406000kling_20260222_VIDEO_Image3_Ima_835_0-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

## [ _app.klingai.com/global_](https://app.klingai.com/global)

* * *

**Pipeline:**

  1. Garment development in CLO3D

  2. High-quality rendering in KeyShot (controlled lighting + consistent camera angle)

  3. Exported 7 sequential still images

  4. Motion generation & interpolation in Kling AI




![7bcb8f096a454d74b06a391d50fb753f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/7bcb8f096a454d74b06a391d50fb753fScreenshot%20%281132%29.png) ![d1eb6c1e3be64ad0bf0c36a42f486a70](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/d1eb6c1e3be64ad0bf0c36a42f486a70gandr-collage%20%2845%29.jpg)

![c86f30bcb6dd4b4c91bd683cb979d1af](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/cd9cef3be4d84498b3937abc971fdbe3/images/c86f30bcb6dd4b4c91bd683cb979d1afScreenshot%20%281133%29.png)

My goal was to test how AI interprets:

  * Fabric weight and drape

  * Surface details and ornamentation

  * Layered silhouettes

  * Continuity of body posture




Using rendered frames instead of raw CLO viewport output helped maintain material realism and lighting consistency during AI interpolation.

This workflow could be useful for:

  * Quick fashion motion previews

  * Concept animation without full simulation

  * Social media content production

  * Early-stage visual storytelling




I’m curious — would you integrate AI motion tools into your CLO workflow, or keep simulation and AI pipelines separate?


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: wow thanks for sharing the pipeline! I'm just keep using the simulation in Marvelous Designer and use AI pipelines after it. But the tech changes really fast these days. So I'm trying to adjust myself to AI environment more than I'm doing it now.
content_description: This web page showcases an innovative workflow that transforms static fashion images into dynamic animations using CLO3D, KeyShot, and Kling AI, highlighting the potential for enhanced visual storytelling in the fashion industry.

title: Technical Issue: Registering and Applying Custom zipper teeth OBJ
content:
Hello CLO Team,

I am currently working on a high-fidelity 3D garment and need to implement a specific custom zipper element shaped like a "baseball home plate" to match a live-action reference. I have s the high-detail tooth in an external 3D software and exported it as a clean .OBJ file.

**The Problem:** Despite multiple attempts to register this OBJ as a custom zipper element, the software is not allowing me to use the custom geometry for the zipper teeth.

**Steps I have already taken:**

  1. **OBJ Preparation:** Exported a single tooth at the correct scale (mm) and ensured the normals are facing correctly.

  2. **Registration Attempt:** I accessed the "Register OBJ" window. However, the "Type" dropdown only provides options for Slider, Puller, and Stopper.

  3. **Library Limitation:** When I register the file as a "Stopper," it saves as a **.zst** file. Because it is a .zst, it does not appear in the **Property Editor > Teeth > Type** dropdown menu when the zipper is selected.

  4. **Menu Search:** I have searched for a specific "Register Zipper Element" or "Register Teeth" option in the Material > Zipper menus but cannot find a dedicated tab for it.




**My Goal:** I need to know if it is possible in this version of CLO3D to register a custom zipper tape teeth as OBJ and replace it with the current obj zipper teeth so it can be populated along the entire length of the zipper path.

![fb104e63bc604259914ff1835e47ba9c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/117a9d3bdc764c3582274e0b9712981e/images/fb104e63bc604259914ff1835e47ba9cimage.png)this is the custom obj teeth i want (i have a single teeth OBJ file which i even imported but it isnt working)  
![139863ddc0384b3c8de484b4627fd1c7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/117a9d3bdc764c3582274e0b9712981e/images/139863ddc0384b3c8de484b4627fd1c7image.png)Please help me with this i am not able to replace it i tried everything


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi.Currently there is no option for registering custom zipper teeth in CLO. But there have been feature requests and our team is aware of the need.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to seek assistance from the CLO Team in resolving the issue of registering a custom "baseball home plate" shaped zipper tooth as an OBJ file within CLO3D software.
